feedback: If a learner treats the larva and adult as two different animals, track one named individual through all four stages as the same insect.
If surprised that a maggot becomes a fly, connect to the familiar caterpillar-to-butterfly case to show the shared pattern.
Reinforce: 'They look completely different because the body was reorganised inside the pupa.'
activities.intendedInsight: The larva looks nothing like the adult because the body is rebuilt in the pupa — but it is the same insect transformed, not a separate creature.
learnerActions: Match each larva to the adult it becomes: maggot→fly, grub→beetle, caterpillar→butterfly.
For each pair, explain why the larva and adult look so different: the body was reorganised inside the pupa.
State that the larva and adult are the SAME individual at different stages, not two different animals.
activities.title: Match the young to the grown-up

feedback: A fully correct response orders the four stages, assigns larva = eat/grow and pupa = transform, gives two examples, and recognises the grasshopper as NOT complete metamorphosis.
If a learner names and orders the stages but can't assign functions, that is partial understanding — probe: 'Why does the caterpillar eat so much before the pupa?'
If a learner calls the grasshopper complete metamorphosis, point out it has no pupa and its young already resemble the adult.
activities.intendedInsight: Understanding is shown by assigning the correct function to each stage and by recognising that an insect with no pupa (young resembling the adult) is NOT complete metamorphosis — not merely by reciting the order.
learnerActions: State the four stages in the right order: egg → larva → pupa → adult.
Say in which stage the insect does most of its eating and growing (larva) and in which stage its body is being rebuilt (pupa), and explain how you know.
Give at least two insects that undergo complete metamorphosis (e.g. butterfly and beetle).

Consider a counterexample: a grasshopper hatches as a young grasshopper (a nymph) that looks like a small adult without working wings, and it grows by shedding its skin several times, with wings developing gradually and no pupa — decide whether that is complete metamorphosis and justify your answer.
activities.title: Which stage does which job?
